title: Ringed-topos pullback of a flat module sheaf
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C\prime$ be small sites, $\mathcal O,\mathcal O\prime$ sheaves of commutative rings on them, and $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C\prime)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ a morphism of topoi, meaning an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ whose left adjoint preserves finite limits. Give a ring-sheaf homomorphism $c:u^{-1}\mathcal O\to\mathcal O\prime$. For a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], put $u^*F=u^{-1}F\otimes_{u^{-1}\mathcal O}\mathcal O\prime$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If $F$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], then $u^*F$ is a flat $\mathcal O\prime$-module sheaf. No flatness of $c$ is assumed. Tensor product is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and flat module sheaf is [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Apply the ringed-site presentation to the given morphism $u$, obtaining the commuting square with ringed equivalences $g,e$ and a site morphism $h$ induced by $v:\mathcal D'\to\mathcal C'$ preserving finite limits. Write $A=\mathcal O_{\mathcal D'}$, $B=\mathcal O_{\mathcal C'}$ and $M=e_*F$.

An equivalence of sheaf topoi preserves kernels, cokernels, and the universal property of balanced bilinear maps, hence induces an exact equivalence of ring-module categories preserving their tensor products. Thus the functor $-\otimes_A M$ is the conjugate by $e_*$ of $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}F$, and is exact. The ringed commuting square identifies $g_*(u^*F)$ with $h^*M$; exactness and tensor preservation for $g$ reduce the conclusion to flatness of $h^*M$.

For a sheaf $T$ on $\mathcal D'$, put $P_T(U)=\varinjlim_{(V,\phi:U\to v(V))\in\mathcal I_U^{\mathrm{op}}}T(V)$, first on underlying sets. This index is filtered since $v$ preserves finite limits, and $h^{-1}T=P_T^\#$. Finite-product preservation defines addition, multiplication and scalar action on these colimits from their stage maps. Sheafification gives $A'=h^{-1}A=P_A^\#$ and $G=h^{-1}M=P_M^\#$ with their ring and module structures; the algebraic sheafification statements identify their underlying sheaves of sets with the set sheafifications.

Fix $U$, $n\geq0$, $a_p\in A'(U)$ and $s_p\in G(U)$ with $\sum_p a_ps_p=0$. Local sheafification first lifts all these finitely many sections to $a'_p\in P_A(U)$ and $s'_p\in P_M(U)$, after successive covering refinements; its local equality assertion then makes $\sum_p a'_ps'_p=0$ in $P_M(U)$ on another refinement. Filteredness and the elementwise colimit statements put all representatives at a common pair $(V,\phi)$, and eventual equality puts the zero relation at a later pair. Denote the final representatives $a''_p\in A(V)$ and $s''_p\in M(V)$: $\sum_p a''_ps''_p=0$. Transition maps preserve sums and scalar products, so this relation has exactly the original images. For $n=0$, choose the pair given by the final object of $\mathcal D'$; the relation is the empty zero sum.

proof.text: Since $M$ is flat, the local equational criterion gives a covering $\{V_i\to V\}$, sections $b''_{ipq}\in A(V_i)$ and $t''_{iq}\in M(V_i)$ such that $s''_p|_{V_i}=\sum_q b''_{ipq}t''_{iq}$ and $\sum_p a''_p|_{V_i}b''_{ipq}=0$.

Set $U_i=U\times_{\phi,v(V)}v(V_i)$. Continuity sends the covering to $\{v(V_i)\to v(V)\}$, and the site base-change axiom makes $\{U_i\to U\}$ a covering. The pair $(V_i,U_i\to v(V_i))$ gives sections $b_{ipq}$ and $t_{iq}$ of $A'$ and $G$ on $U_i$. Their maps preserve sums and scalar products, and the defining equality of the fibre product identifies the image of $s''_p|_{V_i}$ with $s_p|_{U_i}$ and that of $a''_p|_{V_i}$ with $a_p|_{U_i}$. Consequently $s_p|_{U_i}=\sum_q b_{ipq}t_{iq}$ and $\sum_p a_p|_{U_i}b_{ipq}=0$. The reverse implication of the criterion proves that $G$ is flat over $A'$.

proof.text: For every $B$-module sheaf $N$ the balanced tensor universal property gives $(G\otimes_{A'}B)\otimes_B N\cong G\otimes_{A'}\operatorname{Res}N$: on local pure tensors $(g\otimes b)\otimes n\mapsto g\otimes bn$, with inverse $g\otimes n\mapsto(g\otimes1)\otimes n$. Restriction of scalars leaves underlying abelian sheaves, kernels and cokernels unchanged, so is exact. Exactness of a sequence of $B$-module sheaves is detected on its underlying abelian sheaves, by the same kernel and cokernel descriptions. Thus composing restriction of scalars with the exact tensor functor of $G$ and using the displayed comparison shows $G\otimes_{A'}B=h^*M$ is flat over $B$. Step 2 then proves flatness of $u^*F$ without a flatness hypothesis on the coefficient map.
